A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MU-Mis and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Despite substantial expansion and reorganization, the retained and revised content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments, timing comparisons, loss ablations, attention maps, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, sequential-unlearning experiments, hyperparameter studies, ablations, and diagnostic analyses in Section V and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The basic sensitivity-gap objective remains, but Algorithm 1 replaces v1's loss-change stopping criterion with a criterion tracking recovery of irrelevant-class sensitivity relative to its initial value and minimum. Appendix C-D also introduces dynamic loss reweighting, using kappa=80 for Tiny ImageNet and early sequential subclass requests. These alter termination and optimization, rather than merely documenting the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny ImageNet, SVHN, and the Lamp subclass evaluation while retaining the earlier datasets and task families. It also introduces sequential deletion of five distinct classes or five related subclasses. These scenarios add the requirement that previous forgetting survive subsequent unlearning requests, which v1 does not evaluate.

E2.justification: v2 retains v1's five comparators, with Blindspot renamed Bad Teacher (BT), and adds Boundary Expand, EU-k, CF-k, SCRUB, DUCK, SalUn, NG, RL, JiT, and SCAR in reported comparisons. Boundary Shrink also enters subclass comparisons, where v1 excluded it. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: Random-subset deletion changes from 100 CIFAR-10 samples to 10%. v2 adds VGG-16 and ImageNet-initialized ViT configurations, test accuracy, average-gap and output KL-divergence metrics, and sequential-request evaluation procedures. Reported MU-Mis learning rates also differ from v1's stated range. These are substantive evaluation changes, separate from newly disclosed implementation details.

E4.justification: v2 adds sequential-unlearning robustness analyses examining recovery of forgotten knowledge and accumulated utility damage, plus learning-rate and stopping-threshold studies in Figures 4–7 and 9. The attention-map and pairwise-gradient analyses are retained. The loss ablation is revised: v1's two-stage TC-then-OC experiment is removed, as is its Appendix A.2 trajectory comparing forgetting-data and remaining-data sensitivity gaps.

E5.justification: v1 presents point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts or uncertainty. v2 introduces means and standard deviations over five independent trials in Table I and carries this reporting format into other benchmark tables. This is a substantial change in statistical reporting; v1 supplies no prior run count from which an increase in repetitions could be established.

E6.justification: Benchmark results are extensively revised and expanded. For CIFAR-20 Sea, MU-Mis forgetting accuracy changes from 97.66 to 81.00 ± 2.95, while the retrained reference changes from 97.05 to 80.93 ± 2.20 (v1 Table 4; v2 Table II). New architecture, dataset, sequential-unlearning, and hyperparameter results add substantial findings. Changed protocols and reference models prevent interpreting these revisions as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The central contribution/residual decomposition is retained. v2 explicitly states approximations neglecting probability derivatives and changes in the training-dependent gradient mapping, distinguishes infinitesimal self-influence from leave-one-out memorization, and adds an MLP/ReLU derivation in Section III-B, Eqs. (6)–(7). These are limited mathematical extensions and refinements within the existing approximate theoretical framework.

C1.justification: v1 already claims effective, efficient unlearning without remaining data. v2 adds an explicit claim to be the first remaining-data-free method to outperform state-of-the-art methods using remaining data, alongside claims of sequential-unlearning resilience and easy hyperparameter tuning. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion thus expand the claimed novelty and practical capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of sequential failures as knowledge recovery, knowledge residue, and utility breakdown, and connects input sensitivity to generative classifier interpretations and privacy. It acknowledges weaker random-subset competitiveness of remaining-data-free methods. Conversely, v1's concluding limitations about unexplained utility preservation and imperfect contribution estimation disappear, although v2 still describes the sensitivity surrogate as approximate.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds training schedules, optimizers, batch sizes, frozen batch-normalization instructions, baseline implementation sources, and extensive hyperparameter settings and search ranges. Hardware changes from RTX 2080Ti to RTX 4090. Much of this is newly disclosed information rather than demonstrated changes to earlier procedures. v1's promise to release MU-Mis code is absent; v2's implementation links identify baseline sources.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated remaining-data-free related-work subsection positioning MU-Mis against JiT and SCAR. It substantially expands connections to influence estimation, sequential-unlearning evaluation, input curvature, memorization, privacy, and generative interpretations of classifiers. These change the research positioning beyond citation formatting or publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around remaining-data-free unlearning. v1's unified Method section becomes separate analysis and proposed-method sections; experiments and appendices are reorganized, and the Broader Impacts section is removed. The title and author block also change. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different document template and replaces compact benchmark tables with broader tables containing additional metrics, comparator groupings, and uncertainty displays. v1 Figures 3–4 are combined and expanded into v2 Figure 3; attention maps move from Figure 6 to Figure 8, and the gradient histograms become Appendix Figure A2. New sequential and hyperparameter plots substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's limited evaluation, absent uncertainty reporting, and sparse reproducibility information through broader comparisons, sequential-request tests, five-trial statistics, and Appendix C. These make the central utility and efficiency claims much more assessable. Removing the explicit limitations paragraph and using broad superiority language despite weaker random-subset results in Table A5 are drawbacks, and the theory remains approximate. Nevertheless, the empirical scrutiny and reproducibility documentation constitute a substantial net quality improvement.
